text:
anna-choi: quick follow-up from the synthetic load run — we observed noticeable latency spikes on H100 when the SM-capability gate kicked a soft-fallback to the fallback attention kernel. curious what folks think about tolerable penalty vs. safety of the gate :thinking_face:

mike-ramirez: saw that too. can you paste the metric slice? was it p95/p99 or was the whole distribution shifted?

anna-choi: p50 ~ unchanged, p95 +7ms, p99 +18ms for sequences ~512. tails look bimodal right after a gate flip. attached sample snippet below.

anna-choi: ```
run: synthetic-2026-02-14T09
model: redwood-13B
hw: h100-80gb
path: sm-gated -> soft-fallback
p50_latency_ms: 12.4
p95_latency_ms: 19.9
p99_latency_ms: 30.6
observations: spike clusters in first 30s after gate transition
```

devon: likely causes: (1) extra kernel launch overhead for fallback, (2) per-SM handshake RTT for capability check, or (3) shader JIT/prepare step when falling back to generic kernels.

sylvie: for L4 we saw much smaller penalties, probably because the fallback path is already the primary optimized path there. A100 sits in between.

mike-ramirez: do we have telemetry that breaks down where the time was spent? kernel queue -> kernel run -> memcpy?

infra-bot: test-summary: synthetic-2026-02-14T09, sample-size: 5M tokens, fallback-events: 412, avg-handshake-time: 2.8ms, compile-warmup: 6.1ms (first-time), subsequent warmup: 1.2ms. (see internal dashboard)

anna-choi: that compile-warmup looks like the big offender on p99. hypothesis: soft-fallback triggers a code path that lazily prepares a few kernel variants which hurts the tail.

devon: agreed. implementation detail: the gate currently returns a compatibility token, and runtime lazily instantiates the fallback kernel set when the token first used on a device. we can change to eager-instantiate on probe or prefetch during route decision. tradeoffs: memory + startup CPU vs tail latency.

mike-ramirez: tradeoff question: how much tail penalty are we willing to accept for correctness/safety? can we define a penalty budget per device family (H100/A100/L4)?

sylvie: propose budget: H100 10ms p95 uplift allowed, A100 14ms, L4 6ms — numbers we can tune. if we exceed budget, we should route to compatible variant or rate-limit the gate.

devon: alternative is to change the gate to return one of three outcomes: PASS (use fast kernel), PROVISION (pre-warm fallback on device asynchronously), or FORCED-FALLBACK (use fallback immediately without lazy compile). that gives operator control.

anna-choi: good idea. adds a small handshake field in the probe response like: mode:PASS|PROVISION|FALLBACK and optional prewarm_hint bool.

mike-ramirez: implementation wise, PROVISION would need a new async workqueue item on the device agent. infra cost estimate?

infra-bot: rough estimate: prewarming 1 fallback kernel set per GPU ~ 8-12MB extra device memory and ~6-10ms CPU work at attach time. amortized across long-lived allocations.

sylvie: we should also consider a soft-rate limiter: allow up to N soft-fallbacks per minute before escalating to FORCED-FALLBACK and routing to a conservative model variant. prevents cascade on noisy probes.

devon: telemetry needs: mark events with gate_outcome, prewarm_status, first_use_compile_time, kernel_instantiate_time. also annotate by model, seq_len, and batch_shape.

mike-ramirez: +1 on instrumentation. can we add a lightweight sampling flag so we don't blow up storage? sample 1% of fallback events with full traces.

anna-choi: plan proposal:
- short term (hotfix): set gate to PROVISION for H100 during dedicated experiments, enable prewarm on attach for test fleet, and add sampling 1% full traces.
- medium term: implement three-outcome probe, soft-rate-limiter, and operator-configurable penalty budgets per device family.
- long term: evaluate heuristic to prefer cheap compatible kernel variants over fallback if predicted tail > budget.

sylvie: rollout checklist: canary on 10 devices, run synthetic, monitor p95/p99 and memory pressure. if prewarm causes OOMs, rollback to FORCED-FALLBACK.

mike-ramirez: who owns the quick hotfix? I can take the probe response change and sampling. devon can add the prewarm worker. anna to monitor metrics and coordinate canary.

anna-choi: thanks — I'll open a follow-up RFC with the design bits and the metric schema. I'll also add a short runbook for what to do if we see p99 > budget during canary.

devon: one more thought — we should measure mixed-workload interference. fallback prewarm may push kernel caches and evict optimized kernels. test matrix: pure inference vs mixed-train-infer co-located.

sylvie: noted. adding mixed workload test to the canary matrix.

ops-watchdog: created task INF-7832 to add telemetry flags and the prewarm worker. tagging @oncall for the canary window next week. :white_check_mark:

anna-choi: perfect. will paste RFC link once opened. thanks all :raised_hands:
